svg.text: PART A - bullet <-> bullet: cell (i,j) = overlap( b_i , b_j ), i < j -> net pIJ
bb_hit[k] = OR of every pair containing bullet k (pair (i,j) feeds both i and j)
PART B - bullet <-> tank: cell (T,i) = overlap( tank_T , b_i ) -> net tkT_i (tank box 20x20, always alive)
Fig 6c - Collision Engine (2/3): Bullet-Bullet Pair Matrix (28 cells) and Bullet-Tank Cells (16 cells)
Every cell is the Fig-6a overlap cell. All 44 evaluate in parallel every clock; named nets (pIJ, tkT_I) feed the OR gates on the right.
cell inputs: A = {b_i_x, b_i_y, size_i, b_i_act} B = {b_j_x, b_j_y, size_j, b_j_act} (size = 12 if bN_big else 6)
outputs: bb_hit[7:0] (bit k = bullet k overlaps ANOTHER live bullet) -> Fig 6d sticky BB_MASK
Tank operand = {P1/P2_TANK_POS x,y (Fig 5), w=h=20, act=1}. Bullet operand = b_i.
No owner bit: a bullet that bounces back may hit its own tank (classic tank rules).
Software spawns new bullets 24 px in front of the muzzle, so they do not overlap the shooter on frame 0.
tank_set[t] = tankT_hit (tank T struck this clock)
Which bullet landed (so software can read its big flag: 5 dmg vs 1, and deactivate it):
outputs: tank_set[1:0] and btk_hit[7:0] -> Fig 6d sticky registers.
